question: Can a frilled shringasaurus be kept?

resolutions.conclusion: Yes, if it is taken young enough. The juvenile at the market is alive and eating, which settles it.
resolutions.revisit: It is eating, but it is eating less each week, and the ledger has the same entry four times in nine years -- always a juvenile, never the same one twice.

resolutions.conclusion: No. They are bought young four or five times a decade and none has lived two years; the ledger records the purchases and never a sale, a death or a grown animal. It is not a pet that keeps escaping. It is an animal that does not survive being kept, bought again each time by somebody who was not told.

local_knowledge: The drovers will not take one on the caravan at any price and give no reason beyond that it is bad luck on the road -- which is the right answer arrived at from the wrong direction, and four generations quicker than the ledger arrives at it.
academic_hypothesis: A Narmada zoology would say the animal is territorial and solitary and therefore unsuited to confinement, which is true, correctly reasoned, and stops one step short: it explains the distress and not the deaths.
notes:
The question the Tide Market's ledger was waiting for. Deliberately answerable only by reading a merchant's accounts against the animal in front of you -- neither half settles it, which is this map's argument about local knowledge being right without being able to say why.

It is also the quest's off-ramp from capture. A player who arrives meaning to sell one leaves having worked out that the trade cannot work, and the thing to do with the juvenile is take it back.
